english: Why then does the lord give so many gifts? He who gives nothing has no men. He keeps his men with gifts. Has he given you a gift yet? He gives me meat at the feasts. What will you give when you are a man? I give him my arm and my strength. Now you will be a good fighter. Will a foal fall to me? A swift foal will fall to you.
uncertain: moy in 'h₂r̥Hmóm moy' read as 'my' though it could be 'to me'

english: The old lord has died. Now whom will the men choose? They will choose the boldest. Whom would you choose? I would choose my brother's son. He fears nothing. He is bold. Is he wise? He listens to the old men. Now he will lead us rightly.

Brother, I am tired. I'll lie down. Don't sleep. Enemies come at night. I don't see anything. When wolves come, do shepherds sleep? They don't sleep. We are still the war-band's shepherds. Now I keep awake. My comrade told me (a/the word).
uncertain: spélom moy wéwke: 'told me a tale/the word' - odd last line, possibly 'my comrade said so'

english: Which spear shall I take? This one is heavy and that one sharp. Which do you want? I want the sharp one. The sharp spear breaks quickly. The heavy spear does not break. Now I'll take the heavy one and sharpen it. You choose wisely.

Tonight I eat the man's share. What did you earn? I drove off ten horses, and you three horses. I took the shield of their king. Which is greater? The lord will judge (show) rightly. We will divide the share among ourselves. Divide it and pour mead.
uncertain: kʷíd h₁ím h₁édesi: 'what do you eat' vs 'what did you drive' unclear

english: You vowed ten yearlings. How many yearlings did you drive here? I drove nine yearlings. One yearling sank into the river. Now your boast is not true. I do not deceive you. Shall I go back to the river? Don't go. That is no small deceit. Sit with me at the feast.
uncertain: tód ne péh₂urom dʰéh₁lom: 'that is not a small deceit'? or 'that is a small thing, not deceit'
